evidence.detail: rs/cache/d extends rs/cache/e, implements Runnable, owns socket InputStream/OutputStream state, CRC32, request buffers and multiple R25/R47 linked request queues.
Surviving literals include model_crc/model_version/model_index, anim_crc/anim_version/anim_index, midi_crc/midi_version/midi_index, map_crc/map_version and map-index data.
Surviving diagnostics include "Loading extra files - <n>%", "missing start of file", missing-file/revision errors and the update request rejection marker "Rej: ...".
The fetcher has a start/init method taking the recovered archive/stream-loader type plus Client, then runs the background request/download loop.

proposals.note: OnDemandFetcher is fixed by the threaded socket/CRC/versioned update-fetch role.

evidence.detail: rs/cache/c extends R25 NodeSub (rs/a), matching the request-node inheritance used by the classic on-demand queue subsystem.
The class is a compact mutable request record with request-type/id/state integers, booleans and a byte[] payload, and is the element type returned/queued by rs/cache/d.
rs/cache/d returns rs/cache/c from its completed-request path and passes rs/cache/c through its network/request processing methods.

proposals.note: OnDemandData is fixed by the NodeSub request-record role and exact rs/cache/d queue/consumer relationship.

evidence.detail: rs/cache/e contains only the no-op overridable request hook a(int) plus its constructor, matching the classic on-demand fetcher parent shim.
The child/request-node pairing and this one-method base class reproduce the well-known OnDemandFetcher / OnDemandData / OnDemandFetcherParent hierarchy carried by classic clients.

proposals.note: OnDemandFetcherParent is fixed by the direct parent relationship and the one-method no-op hook surface.
